Chief Judicial Magistrate,

 - Vs -

 S/o.Late.Krishnappa,

 1st main, 3rd block, Nandini

[By Sri.Mohan Raju.. Advocate]
Judgment

The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Sub Inspector of Nandini Layout police
station against the accused for the alleged offence punishable under Section 498A of Ipc.
C.C.34174/20

24 2. In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that, the marriage of the accused with C.W.1-Roopa Nandini Layout Police Station vs Pramod Kumar on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101988047/
1 was a love marriage and accused married C.W.1 on 17.11.2017 at Patelamma Temple,
Varthur, Whitefield and after marriage while C.W.1 resided with accused at her matrimonial home at No.6A/15, 1st main, 7th cross, 3rd block, Nandini Layout,
Bengaluru the accused looked after C.W.1 well for a period of one year and later on the accused with an intention to commit an offence used to abuse and assault C.W.1 for petty reasons and did not look after the family necessities and used to suspect the character of C.W.1.

On 13.06.2024 and on 30.06.2024 during night hours the accused consumed alcohol and physically and mentally harassed C.W.1 and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty and therefore the C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused before the Nandini Layout Police seeking necessary action against him in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No.219/2024 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.
Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn, after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.
4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, before that the accused person appeared before court and was enlarged on bail, meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were C.C.34174/2024 sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused, therefore charge was framed and read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, after understanding the same he denied the same and claimed to be tried, accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5.
In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and 2.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused, as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 7 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.
Consequently, recording of statement of accused as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.
6. Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond were obtained from the accused.

7. In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION Nandini Layout Police Station vs Pramod Kumar on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101988047/
2 1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the marriage of the accused with C.W.1-Roopa was a love marriage and accused married C.W.1 on 17.11.2017 at Patelamma Temple, Varthur, Whitefield and after marriage while C.W.1 resided with accused at her matrimonial home at No.6A/15, 1st main, 7th cross, 3rd block, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru the accused looked after C.W.1 well for a period of one year and later on the accused with an intention to commit an offence used to abuse and assault C.W.1 for petty reasons and did not look after the family necessities and used to suspect the character of C.W.1.

On 13.06.2024 and on 30.06.2024 during night hours the accused consumed alcohol and physically and mentally harassed C.W.1 and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty and thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable C.C.34174/2024 under section 498A of IPC?
2. What Order?

8. My answer to the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the 'Negative'
 Point No.2 : As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS 9.
Point No.1 : In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked two documents on her behalf as Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.

The C.W.1 being complainant as well as victim in this case is examined as P.W.1 and Ex.P.1 and 2 documents got marked on her behalf, as far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name Roopa.
M deposed that her marriage with the accused is a love marriage and their marriage was held at Patelamma Temple, Varthur.

Further she deposed that after her marriage with the accused she was residing at the matrimonial house with the accused and out of wedlock they have a son and they are living together in cordial terms and the accused did not extend any physical and mental harassment towards her.
She further deposed that she deposed that she has not lodged complaint against the accused.

She deposed that when she had been to Nandini Layout PS about 04 months back police took her signatures on two documents and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and police did not draw any mahazar before her presence as per Ex.P.2.

She identified her signature on Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 but she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P-1 and 2 as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court, cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P. failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to Nandini Layout Police Station vs Pramod Kumar on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101988047/
3 summon the other witnesses, during the course of prosecution evidence two documents got marked as Ex.P1 and P.2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, but the prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned in the same, therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused, for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused, for which I answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the 'Negative'.
11. Point No.2:

In view of my findings on point No.1 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused is not found guilty and he is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Secs.498A of IPC.
The bail bond executed by the accused stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused is ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if C.C.34174/2024 preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript revised, corrected and signed & then pronounced in the Open court on this the 07 th day of November, 2024.)
(KESHAVA.K) XXXII Addl.Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru.
